licoes.objectivo: Dar informação extra com relativas explicativas (who, which, whose, where), com as vírgulas e as pausas certas.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Elsa, [who] joined in May, will lead the testing.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Sipho, [whose] team worked on the backup, will do the satellite part.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Tômbwa, [where] the work starts in October, is windier than Namibe.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: The proposal, [which] the board wants in October, needs clear costs.

exercicios.enunciado: Choose the correct sentence.

opcoes.texto: My manager, who has worked here for twenty years, is very patient.
My manager, that has worked here for twenty years, is very patient.
My manager who has worked here for twenty years, is very patient.

exercicios.explicacao: Informação extra: entre duas vírgulas, e nunca com that.

exercicios.enunciado: Which sentence needs commas?

opcoes.texto: Luanda which is the capital of Angola has a new airport.
The man who called you is my boss.
The report that I sent you is ready.

exercicios.explicacao: Só há uma Luanda: a relativa dá informação extra. Nas outras, a relativa diz qual homem e qual relatório.

exercicios.enunciado: "Kagiso, whose company makes our sensors, is very reliable." Whose company is it?
Choose the correct sentence.

opcoes.texto: The proposal, which the board wants in October, is almost ready.
The proposal, the board wants in October, is almost ready.
The proposal, that the board wants in October, is almost ready.

exercicios.explicacao: Na informação extra, o pronome nunca sai.

exercicios.enunciado: A Elsa, que entrou em Maio, é de Benguela.
exercicios.resposta: Elsa, who joined in May, is from Benguela.

exercicios.frase: I'm Nuno. Paulo, who you know from Namibe, will look after the installation plan.
exercicios.enunciado: What will Paulo do?

exercicios.frase: Elsa Mendes, who joined us in May, will be in charge of testing.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, com uma pausa antes e outra depois de "who joined us in May".
Introduce three people from your work, your studies or your family to a new colleague. For each person, add extra information with who, whose or where.
exercicios.frase: whose
exercicios.resposta: Let me introduce my team. Ana, who's been with us for fifteen years, knows every client by name. Mário, whose father started the company, knows its whole history. And our office is in Talatona, where most of our clients are.

exercicios.enunciado: Is it harder to lead people who are older or more experienced than you? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: Yes, a bit, because they know more than you about the work. But it can also be easier: you can ask them for advice. The important thing is to respect their experience and to be honest about what you don't know.

licoes.titulo: Which is why we need you
licoes.objectivo: Comentar uma frase inteira com which e usar relativas com preposição.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: The client signed the contract, [which] is great news.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: I've got two small kids, which [means] I can't travel every month.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: These are the people we work [with].

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: She's the person I report [to].

exercicios.enunciado: "…, o que é óptimo." Em inglês:
exercicios.explicacao: "O que", a comentar uma frase inteira, é which.

exercicios.enunciado: In a formal letter, which version is the most formal?

opcoes.texto: the client for whom we work
the client who we work for

exercicios.enunciado: Choose the correct sentence.

opcoes.texto: These are the people we work with.
These are the people with who we work.
These are the people we work with them.

exercicios.enunciado: "Lerato asked me to lead it, which you probably know." What does "which" refer to?

opcoes.texto: the fact that Lerato asked Nuno to lead the team

exercicios.enunciado: A estrada está fechada, o que quer dizer que temos de planear as viagens.
exercicios.resposta: The road is closed, which means we have to plan the trips.

exercicios.frase: This is Paulo. I've got two small kids, which means I can't travel to Tômbwa every month.
exercicios.enunciado: Why didn't Paulo want to lead the team?

opcoes.texto: He can't travel every month because of his kids.

exercicios.frase: You're the person I learned most from, which is why I wanted to talk to you.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita: "which is why" sem uma pausa longa antes.
Tell me about a difficult conversation you had at work or with your family, or one you need to have. Use which for a whole idea at least twice.
exercicios.frase: which
exercicios.resposta: Last year I had to tell my team that we couldn't take holidays in December, which nobody wanted to hear. I explained the reason: our biggest client needed us, which meant overtime for everyone. I was honest, which helped. We agreed on two days off each in January.

exercicios.enunciado: Should a new team leader talk to each person alone before the first meeting? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: Yes, I think so, because people say more when they're alone. The leader can learn what each person is good at and what worries them. Then the first meeting is easier, which is good for everyone.

licoes.objectivo: Dar a palavra, convidar quem não falou, cortar uma digressão com cortesia, retomar e resumir.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: What's your [take] on this, Elsa?

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Let's [park] that for now and come back to it later.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: [Coming] back to the timeline: is five weeks enough?

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Elsa, we haven't [heard] from you yet.

exercicios.enunciado: A colleague has not spoken yet. Which is the most polite?

opcoes.texto: Elsa, we haven't heard from you yet. What's your take?
Elsa, why are you so quiet?

exercicios.enunciado: A colleague is telling a long story that is off the topic. The best reaction:

opcoes.texto: Great story, but let's park that for now.

exercicios.enunciado: Which sentence sums up a discussion?

opcoes.texto: So, where we are is this: draft by the twenty-second, costs by the twenty-ninth.
Would you like to add anything?

exercicios.enunciado: "Let's park that" means…
Gostaria de ouvir a sua opinião sobre isto, Elsa.
exercicios.resposta: I'd like to hear your view on this, Elsa.

exercicios.frase: This is Lerato. Elsa, we haven't heard from you yet. What's your take on the testing?
exercicios.enunciado: What does Lerato want?

exercicios.frase: I'm Elsa. I think we need two weeks for testing, not one.
exercicios.enunciado: How long does Elsa want for testing?

exercicios.frase: Elsa, what's your take on the testing?
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, com a voz a subir no fim.
You're chairing a meeting about an office move. Open it, give the floor to two people by name, cut one digression politely, invite a quiet colleague, and sum up.
exercicios.frase: haven't heard from you
exercicios.resposta: Morning, everyone. One item: the office move. João, would you like to start with the dates? Ana, how do you see it from the IT side? Sorry, Ana, great story, but let's park that. Rui, we haven't heard from you yet. So, where we are is this: we move on the fifteenth.

exercicios.enunciado: Is it a good idea to ask quiet colleagues for their opinion in a meeting? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: Yes, because quiet people often notice things that others miss. But it's better to ask an easy, specific question first, so they don't feel nervous. In our team, the quietest person usually has the best ideas.

licoes.objectivo: Palavras e colocações de liderança, phrasal verbs de trabalho em equipa, pausas numa frase longa; support e eventual.

exercicios.enunciado: Ligue cada palavra à tradução.
Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: When the manager left, Elsa [took over] the project.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Remember to [back up] your files before the update.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: A good leader [follows through] on every promise.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Team [morale] is high after the Namibe project.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Elsa is ready to [take on] more responsibility.

"um eventual atraso" em inglês:
exercicios.explicacao: Falso amigo: eventual = final, que acaba por acontecer.

exercicios.enunciado: "The team supports Nuno." This means…

opcoes.texto: The team helps and encourages Nuno.

exercicios.enunciado: "Back up" has two meanings. Which sentence is about files?

opcoes.texto: Back up everything on the laptop every day.
Paulo always backs me up in meetings.
Can you back me up on Monday?

exercicios.frase: I'm Nuno. When Lerato was ill, I stepped up and chaired the meetings.
exercicios.enunciado: What did Nuno do when Lerato was ill?

exercicios.frase: Paulo, who was my mentor when I started, backs me up in every meeting, which helps a lot.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, com uma pausa em cada vírgula.
Describe the best leader you have worked or studied with. What did this person do? Use at least one phrasal verb and one clause with who or which.
exercicios.frase: which
exercicios.resposta: The best leader I've had was my first manager, who's now retired. She delegated a lot, which scared me at first, but she always backed us up when something went wrong. She gave honest feedback every Friday and followed through on every promise.

exercicios.enunciado: Can people learn to be leaders, or are leaders born? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: I think people can learn, because leadership is mostly listening, planning and being fair. Some people are more confident, of course. But my best manager told me she was very shy at the start.

licoes.objectivo: Seguir uma reunião rápida a cinco vozes: quem fica com cada tarefa e como a líder conduz a reunião.

exercicios.frase: I'm Bongani. Yesterday I finished the network design for the mine in Limpopo.
exercicios.enunciado: What did Bongani finish yesterday?

opcoes.texto: the network design for a mine

exercicios.frase: This is Lindiwe. The client keeps changing the plan, and I need someone to back me up on Monday.
exercicios.enunciado: What does Lindiwe need?

opcoes.texto: someone to back her up on Monday

exercicios.frase: I'm Thandi. Bongani, could you take that on? You know the bank's systems.
exercicios.enunciado: Why does Thandi choose Bongani?

opcoes.texto: He has no work this week.

exercicios.frase: This is Rajesh. The Durban budget is done. Today I'm starting the costs for the Tômbwa proposal.
exercicios.enunciado: What is Rajesh starting today?

opcoes.texto: the costs for the Tômbwa proposal

exercicios.frase: I'm Sipho. I'm happy to take on the satellite design, but I'll need the wind data from Morro Azul.
exercicios.enunciado: What does Sipho need?

opcoes.texto: the wind data from Morro Azul

exercicios.frase: This is Thandi. Sorry, Rajesh, let's park that, and you two can compare clients over lunch.
exercicios.enunciado: What is Thandi doing?
Why does everyone answer "yesterday, today, any problems"?

opcoes.texto: so that nobody talks too long
because the client wants a report

exercicios.enunciado: Thandi says: "Sipho, you did Namibe, which makes you the obvious person." She is…

exercicios.frase: Quick round: yesterday, today, any problems.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita em voz alta.

exercicios.frase: You did Namibe, which makes you the obvious person.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita em voz alta.
You missed the stand-up. Tell a colleague who took each task, and how Thandi kept the meeting short.
exercicios.frase: who
exercicios.resposta: Bongani, who knows the bank's systems, is backing Lindiwe up on Monday. Rajesh is doing the Tômbwa costs, and Sipho, who worked on the Namibe backup, is taking on the satellite part. Nuno is sending the wind data. Thandi kept it short with a quick round.

exercicios.enunciado: Would a ten-minute stand-up meeting work in your team? Why, or why not?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: I think it would work, because our meetings are usually too long. Ten minutes is enough to know who is doing what. But for big problems, we would still need a longer meeting.

OK, so, I don't know. Let's just talk.
First, whose fault was the problem in Namibe?

No promises of deadlines without to confirm with Paulo.

Morro Azul's new finance director will ask by her.
The new director financial of Morro Azul will ask for her.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.

opcoes.texto: He is kind, and he finds a use for the story.
He lets Paulo finish the story.

exercicios.enunciado: What would happen without the satellite?

opcoes.texto: The price would drop by about 15%, but the risk would go up.

Chair the kick-off of a new project at work, at school or in your community: the objective and the time, three people with extra information and their roles, and the next steps.
exercicios.frase: who
exercicios.resposta: Welcome. Three items; we'll finish by ten. Our objective is to open the Huambo branch by March. Ana, who managed the Benguela opening, will lead. Rui, whose team does our IT, will set up the systems. Next steps: Ana, the timeline by Friday; Rui, the IT plan by the twentieth.

exercicios.enunciado: Pass on this note to your team, in English: "Para a equipa: 1) A partir de segunda, a reunião de equipa passa para as 8:30. 2) Quem precisar de sair mais cedo avisa o chefe de equipa na véspera. Obrigada a todos. — A directora"
exercicios.frase: First
exercicios.resposta: Our director says two things. First, from Monday, the team meeting moves to eight thirty. Second, if you need to leave early, tell your team leader the day before. She also thanks everyone.
exercicios.contexto: Mediação: a ordem, as razões e o tom da nota.

Describe the best team you've worked or studied in. What made it work?
exercicios.frase: who
exercicios.resposta: The best team I've worked in was at my first job, in a bank in Benguela. Our manager, who was very calm, gave everyone a clear role, which helped a lot. We had a short meeting every Monday, and we always backed each other up when someone was ill.

exercicios.enunciado: You're the new team leader. Delegate three tasks to three colleagues, with a reason for each.
exercicios.frase: I'd like you to
exercicios.resposta: Ana, I'd like you to prepare the budget, because you know the numbers better than anyone. Rui, could you take on the website? You did the last one. And who'd like to organise the client visit? Marta? Great — you know the client well.
